title_vi: Chiếc huy hiệu đỏ của lòng dũng cảm
translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Crane’s impressionist colour imagery, his ironic distance from heroism and his free indirect thought are rendered in vivid, rhythmic Vietnamese; soldier dialogue is plain and colloquial.
decisions.rationale: The book’s effect is in image and rhythm, not in plot.

decisions.decision: Henry says ‘tôi’ to Jim and addresses him ‘anh’; with Wilson, ‘cậu/tớ’.
decisions.rationale: One address system through the quarrels and the retreat.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘skirmishers’ rendered as snipers ‘lính bắn tỉa’ about eight times from unit 157; now ‘lính tản binh’. ‘at last’ was also wrongly attached to the sun’s rays in unit 95.
‘proverbial chicken’ rendered as a fable chicken; it is the headless chicken of the proverb.
‘heraldic wind’ rendered as a badge (‘phù hiệu’); now a wind that heralds the day.
A garbled sentence (unit 783) and a ‘whale’ calque (985) were corrected.
‘ten hundred’ read as ten thousand; it is one thousand.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: The first draft rendered ‘skirmishers’ as snipers about eight times; the term is now fixed through the book.

glossary.source_term: the youth / the tall soldier / the loud soldier / the tattered soldier
glossary.draft_rendering: chàng thanh niên / gã cao lớn (Jim Conklin) / gã lính ồn ào (Wilson) / gã lính rách rưới
glossary.rationale: Crane’s epithets for his unnamed or half-named soldiers are kept as epithets, with the names given where the text gives them.
One term for the enemy side in soldiers’ speech and narration.
The book’s central image, the wound that the youth envies and fears.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #73, an electronic transcription of Stephen Crane’s The Red Badge of Courage (New York: D. Appleton, 1895), the text first published in book form after the abridged newspaper serialisation of December 1894. The Gutenberg page does not name the exact printing and the text was not collated.

unresolved_questions.explanation: A few phrases such as ‘Cá tươi’ for ‘Fresh fish’ remain slightly literal.

title_review.target_title: Chiếc huy hiệu đỏ của lòng dũng cảm
title_review.rationale: The Vietnamese title ‘Chiếc huy hiệu đỏ của lòng dũng cảm’ is this edition’s own rendering; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: the army waking in its camp.
